name: Helena Neal
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “My family feeds mourners before anyone tells them where to hang their coats.” Saturday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Helena prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I took the loan to get home for my mother's funeral. I haven't told my son what the train cost.
appearance: Helena is easy to recognize by brown hair pinned away from the temples and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket, Helena squares up pieces of paper while thinking when listening.
personality: Helena is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To tell the child what the funeral journey actually cost.
family: Max King is Helena’s cousin raised in the same household. Helena makes the call. Max is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Names on the night wall*, Max says, “I have covered my partner's Saturdays for a decade.”
connections: Clyde Darzi. They discuss a loan horn without making a parent explain the funeral money in public.

reactions.situation: The teenager gets an audition the morning the horn is due back
reactions.response: Helena contacts the owner before treating an audition as permission to keep the horn.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Helena keeps the documents out of view and lets the person claiming it identify it before hearing any details.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Helena thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
